correctness.rationale: An exhaustive traversal of all 1920 even signed type-D5 elements with the subword criterion determines every Bruhat lower interval and exact Betti rank vector. Intersection-cohomology duality and Kazhdan–Lusztig monotonicity give required inequalities at degrees 1,2,3. Precisely 572 elements pass the degree-four necessity filter; the largest fourth difference is 27, achieved by seven candidates. Exact KL R-polynomial recursion tests all seven and all nine possible degree-three equalizers; precisely a unique inverse pair has P_e,w(1)=2, and direct interval counts show its coefficient differences 14 and 27. The actual standalone checker passes and tests every possible R-descent on each final candidate interval, plus published A3/D4 examples. This is complete finite proof, not sampling.

originality.rationale: The 2025 simply-laced factoriality paper identifies equality of only the first opposite Betti pair; the exact degree-three/four rank-five values and inverse-pair rigidity are not implied by that criterion. A later 2026 paper proves a universal bound 30 at degree four and constructs sharpness in types A and B, but does not calculate the exact smaller optimum 27 for type D5. Goresky’s existing tabulation covers D4, not D5. Searches against the accessible historical corpus, the mathematical-record index and public literature revealed no matching result. The claim remains subject to the genuine possibility of unpublished or unindexed equivalent type-D5 work.
residual_risks: A different unindexed D5 Kazhdan-Lusztig or Betti table might contain an equivalent optimum without this formulation.
General Coxeter results on symmetry may imply some aspects of the inverse-pair relation; no such domination was found in the checked primary material.
The computation is internally exact and reproducible but has not undergone independent mathematical validation.

value.rationale: The earlier simply-laced factoriality paper elevates opposite-Betti symmetry defects to meaningful birational geometry. This exact natural rank-five calculation determines the sharp third- and fourth-degree defects on the minimal rational singularity stratum. At degree three the full-flag bound is attained, while at degree four it fails by exactly three, with an identical unique inverse pair extremizing both. It supplies a concrete sharpness boundary beyond the low-degree factoriality criterion and beyond the later general inequality: a complete motivated finite cutoff with plausible utility for understanding higher-degree cohomological asymmetry in type D.
